chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Sadir al-Sayrafi who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Shall I feed a beggar whom I do not know to be a Muslim?' He said: 'Yes, give to one whom you do not know to have wilayah or enmity toward the Truth.'
Indeed, God, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'And speak good words to the people' (2:83).
And do not feed one who has declared hostility against something of the Truth, or calls toward something of falsehood.

key_terms.الْبَاطِل: Al-Batil (falsehood) — the opposite of al-Haqq; refers to religious deviation or false authority
key_terms.الْحَقّ: Al-Haqq (the Truth) — in Shia terminology, refers to the true religion and the authority of the Imams
key_terms.نَصَبَ: Nasaba — lit. 'he erected/set up'; in Shia context, 'al-nasib' is one who declares enmity against the Imams (a nasibi)
key_terms.وَلَايَة: Wilayah — spiritual and political allegiance to the Imams of Ahl al-Bayt; here used as a criterion for determining the recipient's religious affiliation

ai.seo_question: Can a Muslim give charity to a non-Muslim or unknown beggar according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Sadir al-Sayrafi asked Imam al-Sadiq (AS) whether it is permitted to give charity to a beggar whose religious identity is unknown. The Imam responded that giving to those with no known wilayah (allegiance to the Imams) or enmity toward the Truth is permitted, citing Quran 2:83. However, the Imam drew a clear line: one should not feed an active opponent of the Truth or a caller to falsehood. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential concern with both universal charity and maintaining social boundaries that protect the community of faith.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Sadeyr Al Sayrafi who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Shall I feed a beggar whom I do not recognise as being a Muslim?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, you can give to the one who is neither recognised with the Wilayah nor enmity towards the Truth.
Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying [2:83] and you shall speak to the people good words,
and do not give to the one who establishes hostility to something from the Truth, or calls towards something from the falsehood’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from Sadir al-Sayrafiy who has said the following:

“I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘I know someone is asking for help, but I do not know if he is a Muslim or not.’ The Imam said, ‘You can give charity to one whom you do not know is a friend or enemy of the truth.
Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, has said, “Say good words to people.” [2:83]
Do not give charity to those who are hostile to the truth or call people to something of falsehood.’”
